Cabernet Franc is a significant contributor to the character of the Bordeaux wine [Chateau Cheval Blanc](/wiki/Chateau_Cheval_Blanc "Chateau Cheval Blanc") from St-Emilion.

In France, Cabernet Franc is found predominantly in the Loire Valley and in the Libournais region of Bordeaux. As of 2000, it was the sixth most widely planted red grape variety in the country. Other areas with significant plantings include the [Bergerac](/wiki/Bergerac_(AOC) "Bergerac (AOC)") and [Madiran](/wiki/Madiran_(AOC) "Madiran (AOC)") *[Appellation d'origine contrôlée](/wiki/Appellation_d%27origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e "Appellation d'origine contrôlée")* (AOCs). By the early 20th century, there were nearly equal plantings of Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc in Bordeaux with around 25,000 [acres](/wiki/Acre "Acre") (10,000 [ha](/wiki/Hectare "Hectare")) by the late 1960s. Most of these plantings were along the right bank of the [Gironde](/wiki/Gironde "Gironde") in the Fronsac, St-Emilion and Pomerol regions. Towards the end of the 20th century, even though plantings of Cabernet Sauvignon had rapidly increased in Bordeaux to a 2 to 1 ratio in proportion to Cabernet Franc, plantings there were over 35,360 acres (14,310 ha) of the latter, nearly half of the country's total 88,900 acres (36,000 ha).[[4]](#cite_note-Oxford_pg_118-119-4)

In the Loire Valley, Cabernet is widely planted in the [Anjou](/wiki/Anjou_(wine) "Anjou (wine)"), [Bourgueil](/wiki/Bourgueil_(wine) "Bourgueil (wine)"), [Chinon](/wiki/Chinon_(wine) "Chinon (wine)"), and [Saumur-Champigny](/wiki/Saumur-Champigny_(wine) "Saumur-Champigny (wine)") regions.[[4]](#cite_note-Oxford_pg_118-119-4)

The Model Y is a [mid-size crossover SUV](/wiki/Crossover_(automobile) "Crossover (automobile)") offered in 5- and 7-passenger configurations with a single‐motor, rear-wheel drive or a dual-motor, all-wheel drive layout. The vehicle was designed to be more affordable than the luxury Model X SUV. A prototype Model Y was first shown in March 2019,[[73]](#cite_note-electrek-2019-03-14-74) and deliveries started in March 2020.[[75]](#cite_note-Dow_2020-76) The Model Y shared around 75 percent of its content with the Model 3.[[74]](#cite_note-:3-75) In the first quarter of 2023, the Model Y outsold the [Toyota Corolla](/wiki/Toyota_Corolla "Toyota Corolla") to become the world's best-selling car, the first electric vehicle to claim the title.[[127]](#cite_note-128)

Native American languages are spoken in smaller pockets of the country, but these populations are decreasing, and the languages are seldom widely used outside of reservations. Besides English, Spanish, French, German, [Navajo](/wiki/Navajo_language "Navajo language") and other Native American languages, all other languages are usually learned from immigrant ancestors that came after the time of independence or learned through some form of education.

[American Sign Language](/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") is the most common [sign language](/wiki/Sign_language "Sign language") in the United States, although there are unrelated sign languages that have also been developed in the States and territories—mostly in the Pacific. No concrete numbers exist for signers but something upwards of 250,000 is common.
The [most widely taught foreign languages](/wiki/List_of_most_commonly_learned_foreign_languages_in_the_United_States "List of most commonly learned foreign languages in the United States") in the United States, in terms of enrollment numbers from kindergarten through university [undergraduate education](/wiki/Undergraduate_education "Undergraduate education"), are Spanish, French, and [German](/wiki/German_language_in_the_United_States "German language in the United States"). Other commonly taught languages include [Latin](/wiki/Latin "Latin"), [Japanese](/wiki/Japanese_language_education_in_the_United_States "Japanese language education in the United States"), [American Sign Language](/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language"), [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language_in_the_United_States "Italian language in the United States"), and [Chinese](/wiki/Chinese_language_in_the_United_States "Chinese language in the United States").[[18]](#cite_note-19)[[19]](#cite_note-20)

Facebook's rapid growth began as soon as it became available and continued through 2018, before beginning to decline. Facebook passed 100 million registered users in 2008,[[138]](#cite_note-138) and 500 million in July 2010.[[139]](#cite_note-500_million-139) According to the company's data at the July 2010 announcement, half of the site's membership used Facebook daily, for an average of 34 minutes, while 150 million users accessed the site by mobile.[[140]](#cite_note-Quiet_revolution-140)

In October 2012, Facebook's monthly active users passed one billion,[[141]](#cite_note-One_billion_users-141)[[142]](#cite_note-142) with 600 million mobile users, 219 billion photo uploads, and 140 billion friend connections.[[143]](#cite_note-Billion_statistics-143) The 2 billion user mark was crossed in June 2017.[[144]](#cite_note-144)[[145]](#cite_note-145) In November 2015, after skepticism about the accuracy of its "monthly active users" measurement, Facebook changed its definition to a logged-in member who visits the Facebook site through the web browser or mobile app, or uses the [Facebook Messenger](/wiki/Facebook_Messenger "Facebook Messenger") app, in the 30-day period prior to the measurement. This excluded the use of third-party services with Facebook integration, which was previously counted.[[146]](#cite_note-146)

From 2017 to 2019, the percentage of the U.S. population over the age of 12 who use Facebook has declined, from 67% to 61% (a decline of some 15 million U.S. users), with a higher drop-off among younger Americans (a decrease in the percentage of U.S. 12- to 34-year-olds who are users from 58% in 2015 to 29% in 2019).[[147]](#cite_note-Heeti-147)[[148]](#cite_note-Statt-148) The decline coincided with an increase in the popularity of Instagram, which is also owned by Meta.[[147]](#cite_note-Heeti-147)[[148]](#cite_note-Statt-148) The number of daily active users experienced a quarterly decline for the first time in the last quarter of 2021, down to 1.929 billion from 1.930 billion,[[149]](#cite_note-149) but increased again the next quarter despite being banned in Russia.[[150]](#cite_note-150)

In 2011, incumbent U.S. Senator [Daniel Akaka](/wiki/Daniel_Akaka "Daniel Akaka") announced his retirement at the end of his term in 2013. Subsequently, on May 19, 2011, Hirono announced her candidacy for Akaka's seat.[[36]](#cite_note-36) She won the Democratic primary election on August 11, 2012.[[37]](#cite_note-:0-37) Hirono was endorsed as one of the [Dean Dozen](/wiki/Dean_Dozen "Dean Dozen"), a group of candidates chosen for their progressive values by [Democracy for America](/wiki/Democracy_for_America "Democracy for America"), an organization founded by former Vermont governor [Howard Dean](/wiki/Howard_Dean "Howard Dean"). The Republican nominee was former Hawaii Governor [Linda Lingle](/wiki/Linda_Lingle "Linda Lingle"), who had defeated Hirono a decade earlier in the gubernatorial election. Hirono defeated Lingle with 63% of the vote.[[38]](#cite_note-38) She is the first female senator from Hawaii, as well as the first Asian-born immigrant to be elected to the U.S. Senate.[[39]](#cite_note-39) She was a part of the first completely non-Christian congressional delegation from the state, which existed until the election of [Mark Takai](/wiki/Mark_Takai "Mark Takai") (an [Episcopalian](/wiki/Episcopalian_church_in_the_United_States "Episcopalian church in the United States")) in 2014 as the representative for Hawaii's 1st congressional district.[[40]](#cite_note-40)

In the 2012 campaign, Hirono raised $5.2 million, with approximately 52% raised from large corporations. Lingle raised $5.5 million, with 74% from large corporations. Hirono spent $5 million and Lingle $4.8 million.[[41]](#cite_note-41)

Main article: [2018 United States Senate election in Hawaii](/wiki/2018_United_States_Senate_election_in_Hawaii "2018 United States Senate election in Hawaii")
